Introducing EchoRegent:
the context management layer
LLMs were missing.

By Ashmith Atmuri · June 2024 · 6 min read

Every LLM call you make sends the full conversation history. Most of it is noise. You're paying for it anyway. We built a layer that strips the noise before it reaches the model — and makes the answers better.

The problem

When you build a conversational AI product, your context window fills up fast. By turn 10, you're sending a wall of text to the LLM — most of which is pleasantries, re-explanations, and conversational filler from earlier in the session.

You pay for every token in that window. The model's attention degrades as the context gets longer. And you have no idea what domain the conversation is in, so you can't make smart decisions about what to preserve.

What EchoRegent does

EchoRegent sits between your application and the LLM. Before every API call, it runs three small models on CPU — no GPU, no external calls:

1 — Classify

DistilBERT reads the conversation and returns domain (coding, medical, legal, etc.), intent, risk level, and emotional state. In under 10ms.

2 — Compress

T5 summarises the conversation history using a domain-aware strategy. Stack traces compress aggressively. Medical notes don't compress at all. 64.7% average reduction.

3 — Cache & Forward

MiniLM checks for semantically similar past queries. Cache hit → skip compression, return immediately. Cache miss → forward compressed context to your LLM.

The integration

We made the integration as close to zero-friction as possible. If you're using the OpenAI client, you change one URL:

// Before
const client = new OpenAI({ apiKey: "sk-..." })

// After — that's it
const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: "sk-...",
  baseURL: "https://api.echoregent.ai/v1",
  defaultHeaders: { "x-cts-key": "your-echoregent-key" }
})

Protected zones

One design decision we're particularly serious about: medical, legal, and crisis conversations are never compressed. Not configurable. Not overridable by API callers.

When the classifier returns medical, legal, or crisis, the compression step is skipped at the function level. The full context goes to your LLM. Protected conversations are not counted toward your token quota.

What remains

The tagline is "What Remains." That's the literal output — what remains after noise is removed. It's also a philosophy: what should remain in a conversation history is the signal, not the padding. EchoRegent's job is to tell the difference.
